steps: Beta-blocker (propranolol) for symptomatic relief of adrenergic symptoms.
Antithyroid drug — carbimazole (or PTU in 1st-trimester pregnancy).
Determine cause (Graves vs nodular vs thyroiditis) — TRAb, uptake scan.
Discuss definitive options: radioactive iodine or surgery.
Monitor TFTs and FBC/LFTs (agranulocytosis, hepatotoxicity warning).

drugRefs.dose: 10–40 mg three to four times daily, titrated to symptoms/heart rate
drugRefs.why: Rapidly controls adrenergic symptoms (tremor, palpitations, anxiety) while antithyroid therapy takes effect; non-selective and also reduces peripheral T4→T3 conversion at higher doses.

drugRefs.dose: 20–40 mg daily initially, then titrated (or block-and-replace)
drugRefs.freq: once daily (or divided), titrated to TFTs
drugRefs.why: First-line thionamide that inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis. Warn about agranulocytosis (seek help if fever/sore throat) and monitor FBC/LFTs.

drugRefs.dose: 100 mg three times daily (200–400 mg/day), titrated
drugRefs.why: Preferred thionamide in the first trimester of pregnancy (lower teratogenic risk than carbimazole). Carries a risk of hepatotoxicity.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Hyperthyroidism and Thyrotoxicosis
ATA Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism and Other Causes of Thyrotoxicosis

confirm: Weight loss, tremor, heat intolerance, palpitations with suppressed TSH and raised free T4/T3 (uncomplicated, no storm).
